newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia conservatives say may join government.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia conservatives say may join government.

text.p: Slovenia's conservative People's Party said on Monday it was considering forming a coalition with the leading centre-left Liberal Democrats of prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek.
"We support a government of national unity in which all or most parliamentary parties would be included," People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik told a news conference.
Podobnik said the decision would have to be confirmed by the party's governing council, probably later this week.
He did not say when he would meet Drnovsek, who won a fresh mandate to form Slovenia's third government since independence from Yugoslavia in 1991 in a parliamentary vote last Thursday.
Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats won 25 of 90 parliamentary seats in an inconclusive general election last November. He has to present his government lineup to parliament by January 24.

"I will try very seriously to enlarge coalition and form a broader government," Drnovsek said following the parliamentary vote. "According to the election result it would be most appropriate to reach a coalition agreement with the People's Party," he said in an invitation to Podobnik to join coalition talks.

Podobnik, whose party won second place in the election with 19 seats, had ruled out working with Drnovsek before the parliamentary vote but his comments on Monday suggested his party was re-thinking its position.

Podobnik leads an alliance of three rightwing parties that had hoped to oust the prime minister and form an administration themselves. But the defection of a deputy from the Christian Democrats to Drnovsek's side scuppered the hopes of the alliance.

Drnovsek won the vote in parliament with the slimmest of margins by 46 votes against 44, with support from smaller parties, including former communists. But the premier knows he would have an easier time pushing through economic reforms if he had the right on his side in a coalition.
